newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher, investors focus on Sulzer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher, investors focus on Sulzer.

text.p: Swiss shares recovered from a dip below 4,000 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) around midday to end slightly higher as investors concentrated on diversified engineering group Sulzer.
Shares in Sulzer soared around 17 percent on plans to sell-off some 25 percent of its Sulzer Medica unit, a move seen as favourable for the group.
Sulzer shares jumped 144 francs to 982 after reaching an all-time high of 1,000 francs in early trade.
The blue-chip SMI ended 13.7 points, or 0.34 percent, higher at 4,023.2 and the broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended at 2,581.43 points, up 6.76 points, or 0.26 percent, from Monday's close.
Nestle added six francs to 1,475, although the 7.1 percent rise in 1996 group sales to 60.5 billion francs was within expectations, a trader noted.
Nestle also expected profit growth in 1996 to exceed growth seen in sales.
Dealers said U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's speech before the Senate Budget Committe was well received by markets. Trading volumes were described as relatively high.
Future development depended largely on Wall Street's moves, a trader noted.

UBS outperformed the other major banks on a recommendation by Lehman Brothers, a dealer said. UBS bearer shares added 18 francs, or 1.58 percent, to 1,155 francs. CS Holding eased 0.75 francs to 137.75. SBC gave up 0.25 francs to 247.50.
Among insurers, Winterthur profited from its 2.5 percent stake in Sulzer, dealers said. Winterthur rose 15 francs, nearly two percent, to 793.
